mcqs.question: Who won the Thomas Cup at the 2026 Thomas and Uber Cup Finals held at Forum Horsens, Denmark?
mcqs.explanation: China won the 2026 Thomas Cup and secured its 12th title. France was the runner-up, while India and Denmark won the bronze medals; South Korea won the Uber Cup, not the Thomas Cup.

mcqs.question: Who was appointed Chef de Mission of India for the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow?
mcqs.explanation: Rohit Rajpal was appointed India’s Chef de Mission for the 2026 Commonwealth Games. Ravi Bengani was the Deputy Chef de Mission, while Vandana Rao and Rahul Swamy were team managers.

mcqs.question:
India was awarded the 2027 Asian Relays and the 2028 Asian Indoor Athletics Championships.

Statement A: The 2027 Asian Relays will be held at the Sector-7 Sports Complex in Chandigarh.
Statement B: The 2028 Asian Indoor Athletics Championships will be held at Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The 2027 Asian Relays were assigned to the Sector-7 Sports Complex, Chandigarh, while the 2028 Asian Indoor Athletics Championships were assigned to Kalinga Stadium, Bhubaneswar.

mcqs.question: With reference to the Asian Weightlifting Championships 2026 held in Gandhinagar, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: India won 10 medals, comprising 1 silver and 9 bronze medals.
China’s medal tally comprised 21 gold, 12 silver and 9 bronze medals.
Gyaneshwari Yadav won silver in the women’s 53 kg snatch.
China topped the medal table with 41 medals.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that China won 9 bronze medals. China’s 41-medal tally comprised 21 gold, 12 silver and 8 bronze medals; the other statements correctly describe India’s haul and Gyaneshwari Yadav’s silver.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Gurindervir Singh set the 100 m national record with a time of 10.09 seconds at the 29th National Senior Athletics Federation Cup in Ranchi.
Reason (R): The record was broken twice in 48 hours.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Assertion A is true: Gurindervir Singh clocked 10.09 seconds on 23 May 2026 at the Ranchi event. Reason R is false because the record was broken three times in 48 hours, progressing from Gurindervir Singh’s 10.17 seconds to Animesh Kujur’s 10.15 seconds and then 10.09 seconds.

mcqs.question: Whom did Sourabh Kothari defeat in the final to retain the IBSF World Billiards title?
mcqs.explanation: Sourabh Kothari defeated Pankaj Advani 1133–477 in the final and defended his 2025 title. Manoj Kothari is Sourabh Kothari’s father and an ex-world champion, while the other two options are associated with athletics.

mcqs.question:
With reference to the National Sports Board and Tribunal Rules, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The Rules were notified under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025.
2. The National Sports Board recognises National Sports Federations and consists of a Chairperson and two members.
3. The National Sports Tribunal provides for online filing and virtual hearings.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The Rules were notified under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025; the Board recognises National Sports Federations and has a Chairperson with two members; and the Tribunal permits online filing and virtual hearings.

mcqs.question: At which venue was Bharat Singh Chauhan re-elected as Chair of the Commonwealth Chess Association for the 2026–2030 term?
mcqs.explanation: Bharat Singh Chauhan was re-elected at the AGM held in Wadduwa, Sri Lanka, for the 2026–2030 term. Lausanne, Bonn and Kuwait City are associated with other sports organisations in the facts, not this AGM.

mcqs.question: Faustino Oro became the second-youngest Grandmaster in chess at approximately what age?
mcqs.explanation: Argentine prodigy Faustino Oro became a Grandmaster at approximately 12 years, 6 months and 26 days. The age of 12 years, 4 months and 25 days belongs to Abhimanyu Mishra, who remains the youngest Grandmaster.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the proposed transfer of para shooting governance:
1. Para Shooting is to move from the IPC to the ISSF.
2. The new system is scheduled to begin from 2027, with a transition during 2027–28.
3. The ISSF is headquartered in Munich and is headed by Luciano Rossi.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct: para shooting is proposed to move from the IPC to the ISSF, the new system is planned from 2027 with a 2027–28 transition, and the ISSF is based in Munich with Luciano Rossi as President. The agreement still requires approval at the 2026 General Assembly.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding Everest summit records is incorrect?
options: Kami Rita Sherpa’s 32nd Everest summit is the men’s record.
Lhakpa Sherpa’s 10th Everest summit is the women’s record.
Everest is 8,849 metres high and lies on the Nepal–China border.
K2 is the second-highest mountain and lies on the Pakistan–China border.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement changes Lhakpa Sherpa’s record from the 11th summit to the 10th; her 11th summit is the women’s record. Kami Rita’s 32nd summit is the men’s record, while Everest and K2 have the stated heights and border locations.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: NADA imposed a seven-year ban on discus thrower Banveer Singh after extending his earlier five-year suspension by two years.
Statement B: Long-distance runner Harendra Kumar received an additional four-year ban.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Banveer Singh’s earlier five-year suspension was extended by two years to a seven-year ban, while Harendra Kumar received an additional four-year ban.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II in the context of the book on India’s first Olympic hockey gold.

List-I
 a. Author of “India's Olympic Gold: Hockey Triumph at Amsterdam”
 b. Dignitaries who unveiled the book
 c. Year and venue of India’s first Olympic hockey gold
 d. Publisher of the book

List-II
 i. Stick to Hockey
 ii. K. Arumugam
 iii. 1928 Amsterdam
 iv. P.T. Usha and Dilip Tirkey
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-iv, c-iii and d-i: K. Arumugam authored the book, P.T. Usha and Dilip Tirkey unveiled it, India won its first Olympic hockey gold at Amsterdam in 1928, and Stick to Hockey published it. The other codes interchange the author, dignitaries, year and publisher.

mcqs.question: How many medals did India win at the Asian U15 Boxing Championships held in Tashkent, Uzbekistan?
mcqs.explanation: India won 27 medals at the Asian U15 Boxing Championships: 9 gold, 6 silver and 12 bronze. The figures 14 and 13 refer to the medal tallies of the U15 girls’ and boys’ teams respectively, while 9 is only the number of gold medals won by India.
